messages:
sam: Heads up — customer hitting persistent 504s with our Go SDK. They rapidly cancel request contexts and we end up with many goroutines + connections in TIME_WAIT. Quick repro below, minimal app that demonstrates behavior when ctx is canceled during a slow response.

sam: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
client := &http.Client{
    Timeout: 5 * time.Second, // this global timeout + ctx cancel seems to interact badly
    Transport: &http.Transport{
        MaxIdleConns:        100,
        MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
        IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
        TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
    },
}
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", "https://api.redwood.run/slow", nil)
res, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil {
    log.Printf("err: %v", err)
    return
}
io.ReadAll(res.Body)
res.Body.Close()
```

sam: Observed: many goroutines stuck in net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop or waiting on reads; logs show: `context canceled` AND later `Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers`. Connections appear to not be reused for a while.

maria: Can you paste go version + sdk version + any custom dialer or middleware the customer uses? Also their traffic pattern (short-lived ctx cancels vs long polling).

sam: Go: go1.20.6, SDK: v0.13.1, no fancy middleware, direct http.Client via our SDK transport wrapper. Pattern: high QPS of short requests, most are canceled within 200-800ms because upstream does long streaming.

sam: Logs: `2026-03-12T17:02:13Z error: context canceled` followed by `2026-03-12T17:02:18Z warn: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)` and goroutine dump snippets showing many in `(*persistConn).readLoop` and some in `(*http2clientConn).roundTrip`.

akshay: This matches an interaction we've seen: using `Client.Timeout` (which applies to the whole request) AND canceling the Request context can race. When Client.Timeout fires it can return a different error and the transport cleanup path can diverge, leaving connections in odd states. Also, http2 had issues in older stdlib versions where stream resets didn't always free resources immediately.

akshay: Quick mitigation: avoid `http.Client.Timeout` when you already pass context with a deadline. Instead configure the Transport dial/response timeouts explicitly and rely on Request.WithContext. Example patch: 

akshay: ```go
// recommendedTransport returns a transport configured for cancellations
func recommendedTransport() *http.Transport {
    return &http.Transport{
        DialContext: (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 5 * time.Second, KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext,
        MaxIdleConns:        100,
        MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
        IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
        TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
        ResponseHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second, // bound waiting for headers separately
    }
}
// usage: client := &http.Client{Transport: recommendedTransport()}
// do NOT set client.Timeout if you use per-request contexts
```

maria: I ran this locally against the repro — removing `Client.Timeout` and adding `ResponseHeaderTimeout` + Dialer timeout removed the goroutine pile-up in my run. Looks promising.

maria: Are there edge cases for http2 streams? We saw some `http2clientConn` entries in the dump.

lee: Note: Go 1.20 had a couple http2/cancel bugs; upstream fixed many in go1.21+ (stream reset propagation, timely connection reuse). Recommend customers upgrade runtime if possible. For immediate guidance: set `Transport.ForceAttemptHTTP2 = true` (default) but ensure `ResponseHeaderTimeout`/`ReadIdle` are set so streams don't linger.

lee: Also add a short liveness/read timeout on the response body reads in the app logic when doing streaming reads — that prevents long tail goroutines. Example: wrap Body with a reader that respects ctx or use `httptrace` to observe when headers arrive.

sam: Created support ticket SUP-2026 with repro, stack dumps, and metrics. Customer is willing to apply transport tweaks. I'll propose a recommended config snippet and note runtime upgrade.

maria: I'll draft a KB article with the repro, why Client.Timeout+ctx can interact poorly, recommended Transport settings, and go runtime recommendation. Will attach the code sample and suggested config.
